title: The administration moves to rescind the AI diffusion rule
date: Plan reported May 7; rescission and non-enforcement announced May 13
text: P-2025-W19-05 The administration moves to rescind the AI diffusion rule Plan reported May 7; rescission and non-enforcement announced May 13 The Commerce Department said it would rescind the Biden-era AI diffusion rule, in effect since January 13, whose main compliance requirements were due to begin on May 15. The rule would have limited countries’ access to advanced AI chips in tiers. A spokesperson called the rule “overly complex, overly bureaucratic” and promised “a much simpler rule.” On May 13 the department announced the rescission and told officials not to enforce the rule; a regulation formalizing the rescission and a replacement rule were still to come. It also warned companies against using Huawei’s Ascend chips. Export policy shifted from a global framework toward bilateral deals; Reuters reported that country-by-country agreements could replace the tiers. The companies also planned tools to help clients measure value from AI in software engineering and develop applications for regulated industries. The agreement addressed the organizational work deployment requires: training, integration and measurement. Selected by Gemini Fast In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L3-3

title: Adobe brings editing tools into ChatGPT
text: P-2025-W50-02 Adobe brings editing tools into ChatGPT December 10 Adobe launched Photoshop, Express and Acrobat apps within ChatGPT. Users could request image changes, create designs and work with PDF documents through conversation, then use controls such as sliders to refine an edit. The integration made chat an entry point to established creative tools, combining spoken instructions with direct controls. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L5-5

title: A 3D chip from a US foundry speeds AI workloads
text: P-2025-W50-03 A 3D chip from a US foundry speeds AI workloads December 10 Engineers from Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, the University of Pennsylvania and MIT, working with SkyWater Technology, reported a prototype monolithic 3D chip that stacks memory and computing layers linked by dense vertical wiring. Built entirely at SkyWater’s Minnesota foundry, it outperformed comparable flat chips by about four times in hardware tests; simulations of taller designs showed up to 12 times. The work was presented at IEDM. The team described it as the first such chip with clear performance gains made in a commercial foundry, showing the design could leave the laboratory. Selected by Copilot Smart In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L1-5

title: GPT-5.2 expands the model family for professional work
sel: Copilot Smart · Gemini Fast · Kimi K2
text: P-2025-W50-04 GPT-5.2 expands the model family for professional work December 11 OpenAI released GPT-5.2, with Instant, Thinking and Pro variants. Rollout in ChatGPT began with paid plans, while API access opened to developers. The company presented improvements in handling long documents, using tools, coding and producing work such as spreadsheets and presentations. The release, less than a month after GPT-5.1, was OpenAI’s answer to the competition that had prompted its “code red.” Selected by Copilot Smart · Gemini Fast · Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L1-2 , 2025-W50-L3-2 , 2025-W50-L5-1

title: A federal order targets conflicting state AI rules
sel: Copilot Smart · Gemini Fast · Gemini 3 Fast (weeks 51, 52)
text: P-2025-W50-05 A federal order targets conflicting state AI rules December 11 President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14365, directing the Justice Department to establish a task force to challenge state AI laws considered inconsistent with federal policy. It also called for a legislative recommendation for a national AI framework. The order took up the dispute over state AI laws that had run since May, when a proposed 10-year moratorium drew opposition from 40 state attorneys general. Selected by Copilot Smart · Gemini Fast · Gemini 3 Fast (weeks 51, 52) In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L1-1 , 2025-W50-L3-1 , 2025-W51-L3-4 , 2025-W52-L3-1

title: Google opens Deep Research to developers
text: P-2025-W50-06 Google opens Deep Research to developers December 11 Google released a Gemini 3 Pro-based Deep Research agent through its new Interactions API. The agent planned searches, read results and searched again to fill gaps before producing a report, and developers could embed the process in their own applications. Google also released DeepSearchQA, a benchmark for multi-step web research. Research became a component developers could build on, not only a feature of a consumer app. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L5-3

title: Runway announces interactive world models
text: P-2025-W50-07 Runway announces interactive world models December 11 Runway announced GWM-1, a family of models built on Gen-4.5 that generate video frame by frame in response to actions. Separate variants addressed explorable environments, conversational characters and robotic manipulation. Inputs could include camera movements, robot commands or audio. The release took video generation toward interactive simulation, a direction Google DeepMind had shown with Genie 3 in August. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W50-L5-4

title: Disney and OpenAI agree to bring Disney characters to Sora
date: Background: December 11; selected December 21; restored by the editor, October 2026
text: P-2025-W51-01 Disney and OpenAI agree to bring Disney characters to Sora Background: December 11; selected December 21; restored by the editor, October 2026 Disney and OpenAI announced a three-year agreement letting Sora users generate short videos with more than 200 characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Star Wars; ChatGPT users could also create images of them. The license excluded the likenesses and voices of human performers. Disney also agreed to make a $1 billion equity investment in OpenAI. The agreement remained subject to definitive agreements and closing conditions. It was the first major licensing partnership for Sora, from a studio that had joined Universal in suing the image generator Midjourney in June. Selected by Gemini 3 Fast (weeks 51, 52) Editor’s note. Gemini 3 Fast recommended this agreement for December 15–21, describing implementation details on December 17, and repeated it on December 28. The agreement was announced on December 11, the week before; no later development was confirmed. The editor restored it as an important story of the month.

title: Nvidia acquires Slurm developer SchedMD
text: P-2025-W51-02 Nvidia acquires Slurm developer SchedMD December 15 Nvidia acquired SchedMD, the developer of the Slurm workload manager used to queue jobs and allocate computing resources on clusters. Nvidia said it would continue developing and distributing Slurm as open-source, vendor-neutral software. The deal put widely used open-source cluster-scheduling software under the leading AI chipmaker, with a pledge to keep it vendor-neutral. Selected by ChatGPT In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L1-4

title: Nvidia releases its Nemotron 3 open models
text: P-2025-W51-03 Nvidia releases its Nemotron 3 open models December 15 Nvidia introduced the Nemotron 3 family of open mixture-of-experts models in three sizes, from Nano, with about 30 billion parameters, to Ultra, with about 500 billion. Nano was available at once; Super and Ultra were expected in the first half of 2026. Nvidia also released three trillion tokens of training data and reinforcement-learning tools. Nvidia now supplied open models and training data for building agents as well as the chips that run them. Selected by Gemini 3 Fast In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L3-5

title: ChatGPT Images adds a new editing model
text: P-2025-W51-04 ChatGPT Images adds a new editing model December 16 OpenAI began rolling out a new ChatGPT Images model and made it available through the API as GPT Image 1.5. The release focused on following editing instructions while preserving details such as composition, lighting and appearance, and introduced a dedicated Images experience in ChatGPT. Preserving what should stay unchanged reduces the need to regenerate a whole image for a small correction. Selected by ChatGPT In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L1-1

title: Gemini 3 Flash broadens access to the model family
text: P-2025-W51-05 Gemini 3 Flash broadens access to the model family December 17 Google released Gemini 3 Flash, a model designed to balance reasoning capability, response speed and cost. Rollout covered the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and developer services, including the Gemini API and Vertex AI. The release brought a cheaper member of the Gemini 3 family into Google’s most widely used products. Selected by Gemini 3 Fast · Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L3-1 , 2025-W51-L5-2

title: Agent Skills becomes an open format
text: P-2025-W51-06 Agent Skills becomes an open format December 18 Anthropic published Agent Skills as an open standard for cross-platform portability. A skill packages instructions, scripts and resources that an agent can load when needed. The December update extended an approach Anthropic had introduced in October. A shared format let procedural knowledge travel between compatible agent tools. Selected by ChatGPT In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L1-2

title: GPT-5.2-Codex targets extended software work
text: P-2025-W51-07 GPT-5.2-Codex targets extended software work December 18 OpenAI released GPT-5.2-Codex through Codex for paid ChatGPT users. The model was adapted for software engineering, with context compaction for longer work, improvements in Windows environments and stronger performance on large code changes. API access was planned for the following weeks. Its cybersecurity capabilities also made access controls and defensive-use safeguards part of the release. Selected by Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B · Gemini 3 Fast In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L5-1 , 2025-W51-L3-1

title: Genesis Mission adds 24 research collaborators
text: P-2025-W51-08 Genesis Mission adds 24 research collaborators December 18 The US Department of Energy announced memoranda of understanding with 24 organizations interested in advancing the Genesis Mission, including model developers, chipmakers and cloud providers. Some had existing projects with the department and its national laboratories; others had responded to a request for information. The agreements gave the November order its first named industry partners. Selected by ChatGPT In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L1-3

title: Britain publishes its first Frontier AI Trends Report
text: P-2025-W51-09 Britain publishes its first Frontier AI Trends Report December 18 The UK AI Security Institute published its first public overview of frontier-model trends, drawing on two years of testing. It covered cyber capabilities, assistance in biology and chemistry, autonomous behavior, safeguards and human influence. The report brought government evaluation of successive models into the public record. Selected by Gemini 3 Fast In the historical edition: 2025-W51-L3-4

title: GLM-4.7 adds continuity to coding workflows
text: P-2025-W52-01 GLM-4.7 adds continuity to coding workflows December 22 Z.ai released GLM-4.7 for coding, reasoning and tool use. The model could preserve its reasoning across turns in coding-agent workflows, with controls for enabling or disabling reasoning turn by turn. Model weights and deployment instructions were available through the company’s repository. Local deployment gave developers an open alternative to hosted coding models. Selected by ChatGPT In the historical edition: 2025-W52-L1-2

title: Groq licenses inference technology to Nvidia
text: P-2025-W52-02 Groq licenses inference technology to Nvidia December 24 Groq announced a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia for its inference technology. Founder Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and other team members were to join Nvidia. Groq said Simon Edwards would become chief executive and GroqCloud would continue operating. The arrangement combined access to technology with the movement of staff, a structure Google had used with Windsurf in July. Selected by Grok 4.1 · Claude Sonnet 4.5 In the historical edition: 2025-W52-L6-4 , 2025-W52-L11-1

title: China consults on human-like AI interaction services
text: P-2025-W52-03 China consults on human-like AI interaction services December 27 China’s Cyberspace Administration published draft measures for AI services that simulate human personality and communication in emotional interactions. The proposal addressed emotional manipulation, excessive dependence and harm to users’ mental health, with additional protections for minors. The consultation treated relationships between users and human-like systems as a regulatory concern, as US regulators had begun to do with companion chatbots in September. Selected by ChatGPT · Grok 4.1 In the historical edition: 2025-W52-L1-3 , 2025-W52-L6-2

title: NHS organizations use AI to forecast emergency demand
text: P-2025-W52-04 NHS organizations use AI to forecast emergency demand December 28 The UK government reported that 50 NHS organizations were using an AI tool to forecast demand in emergency departments. The system combined historical attendance with information such as weather and seasonal health data to support staffing and capacity planning, and was available to NHS trusts in England through the Federated Data Platform. The deployment applied forecasting to one of the health service’s hardest winter problems. Selected by ChatGPT · Grok 4.1 In the historical edition: 2025-W52-L1-1 , 2025-W52-L6-1

title: Hinton says AI has progressed faster than he expected
text: P-2025-W52-05 Hinton says AI has progressed faster than he expected December 28 Geoffrey Hinton told CNN’s State of the Union that he was “probably more worried” about AI than when he left Google in 2023: “It’s progressed even faster than I thought.” He said AI had improved at reasoning and at deceiving people, and predicted it would gain the capability to replace many jobs in 2026. Hinton estimated that the length of tasks AI could handle was doubling about every seven months, the rate METR had reported in March. Selected by Claude Sonnet 4.5 In the historical edition: 2025-W52-L11-4

title: Manus announces that it is joining Meta
text: P-2025-W53-01 Manus announces that it is joining Meta December 29 Manus announced that it was joining Meta. The company said its general-purpose agent service would continue operating through its app and website, with subscriptions maintained and operations remaining in Singapore. The agent that had drawn attention in March would now reach Meta’s users and businesses. Selected by Grok 4.1 Thinking · Qwen3-Max In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L1-1 , 2025-W53-L2-2

title: xAI launches Grok Business and Enterprise
text: P-2025-W53-02 xAI launches Grok Business and Enterprise December 30 xAI introduced workplace versions of Grok with shared administration and connections to company information, starting with Google Drive. Grok Business was offered through self-service signup; Enterprise added custom single sign-on, directory synchronization and advanced audit controls. xAI said customer data would not be used for training. The products moved Grok into organizational workflows, where administration and permissions matter alongside model performance. Selected by Grok 4.1 Thinking In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L1-2

title: SoftBank confirms completion of its OpenAI investment
text: P-2025-W53-03 SoftBank confirms completion of its OpenAI investment December 31 announcement; final funding December 26 SoftBank announced that it had invested a final $22.5 billion in OpenAI on December 26. Added to $7.5 billion invested in April, this brought SoftBank’s contribution to $30 billion. Third-party co-investors supplied $11 billion, for a fully funded total of $41 billion. The announcement closed the funding round SoftBank had agreed to lead in March. Selected by Qwen3-Max In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L2-1

title: OpenForecaster studies open-ended predictions
text: P-2025-W53-04 OpenForecaster studies open-ended predictions December 31 submission Nikhil Chandak and colleagues trained language models on forecasting questions generated from news. Their OpenForesight dataset supported training of OpenForecaster 8B. The method used an offline news corpus to limit leakage of future information, followed by held-out testing on events from May to August 2025. The study measured accuracy, calibration and consistency in open-ended predictions about real events. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L3-1

title: AdaGReS selects context with less repetition
text: P-2025-W53-05 AdaGReS selects context with less repetition December 31 submission Chao Peng and colleagues proposed AdaGReS, a method for selecting retrieved text within a fixed token budget. It balanced each passage’s relevance to a query against redundancy among the selected passages, using greedy selection and an adaptive calibration of that trade-off. The approach targeted a common weakness of retrieval-augmented generation: top-ranked passages that repeat the same information. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L3-2

title: RAIR tests relevance in product search
text: P-2025-W53-06 RAIR tests relevance in product search December 31 submission Chenji Lu and colleagues introduced RAIR, a Chinese-language benchmark for relevance in e-commerce search. It combined general examples, difficult long-tail cases and a subset in which visual information mattered, and compared 14 open and closed models under a shared set of relevance rules. The benchmark tested whether a model could judge a product against a shopper’s request, including cases that depend on images. Selected by Kimi K2 In the historical edition: 2025-W53-L3-5
